From ffe68c3766997d82e9ccaf1cdbd47eba269c4aa2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thomas Fourier <fourier.thomas@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 17:43:39 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: ethernet: ec_bhf: Fix dma_free_coherent() dma handle

dma_free_coherent() in error path takes priv->rx_buf.alloc_len as
the dma handle. This would lead to improper unmapping of the buffer.

Change the dma handle to priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys.

Fixes: 6af55ff52b02 ("Driver for Beckhoff CX5020 EtherCAT master module.")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Fourier <fourier.thomas@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260213164340.77272-2-fourier.thomas@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/ec_bhf.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/ec_bhf.c
index 67275aa4f65b..0c86cbb0313c 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/ec_bhf.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/ec_bhf.c
@@ -423,7 +423,7 @@ static int ec_bhf_open(struct net_device *net_dev)
 
 error_rx_free:
 	dma_free_coherent(dev, priv->rx_buf.alloc_len, priv->rx_buf.alloc,
-			  priv->rx_buf.alloc_len);
+			  priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys);
 out:
 	return err;
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies one file (`drivers/net/ethernet/ec_bhf.c`) with a single change: correcting the DMA handle argument in a `dma_free_coherent()` call within the error path of the `ec_bhf_open()` function. The original code incorrectly passed `priv->rx_buf.alloc_len` (a buffer size) as the DMA handle, which would cause improper unmapping. The fix replaces it with `priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys` (the actual DMA address), aligning with the expected API usage for proper DMA resource cleanup. This is a straightforward argument type correction without any other structural or functional changes.

Root cause:
The bug is caused by a typo in the error path of `ec_bhf_open()`, where `dma_free_coherent()` was called with `priv->rx_buf.alloc_len` (a buffer size) as the DMA handle argument, instead of `priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys` (the correct DMA address). This results in improper unmapping of the DMA buffer, potentially leading to memory corruption or system instability.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
dma_free_coherent(dev, priv->rx_buf.alloc_len, priv->rx_buf.alloc,
		  priv->rx_buf.alloc_len);
Reason:
In the error path of `ec_bhf_open()`, after a failure allocating the TX buffer, the code attempts to free the previously allocated RX buffer using `dma_free_coherent`. The fourth argument expects the DMA handle (physical address) of the buffer, but `priv->rx_buf.alloc_len` is a buffer size, not an address. This causes incorrect unmapping, potentially leading to memory corruption or system instability.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
-			  priv->rx_buf.alloc_len);
+			  priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys);
Reason:
The corrected line uses `priv->rx_buf.alloc_phys`, which is the proper DMA address returned by `dma_alloc_coherent`. This ensures that the DMA buffer is correctly unmapped and freed.

out:
	return err;
}
